ai_review.summary: A solid 1971 performance highlighted by a powerhouse Good Lovin' and an incredible Not Fade Away → Great Day Tripper → Not Fade Away run, with a short gorgeous Dark Star; recording quality isn’t commented on but the source appears to be a standard soundboard capture.
ai_review.review: The show is generally praised for its high‑energy moments – especially Good Lovin', the NFA>GDTRFB>NFA sequence and a tight Dark Star – while the Playin' in the Band fell flat for some listeners. Reviewers note only two Pigpen numbers (organ/B‑3) and debate whether Ned Lagin is on piano, but overall they consider it a good 1971 show worth hearing.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews are 4‑star and focus on strong musical highlights with minor criticisms; recording quality is not mentioned, so the rating leans on show performance.

recording_quality.technical_notes: No reviewer comments on audio fidelity; filename suggests a soundboard source but this isn’t confirmed in the reviews.

standout_songs: Not Fade Away > Great Day Tripper > Not Fade Away
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set has a few high‑impact peaks (Good Lovin', NFA/GT/Fade, Dark Star) but overall feels uneven for 1971 standards; still regarded as an enjoyable, cohesive performance.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar work on the opening 'I Second That Emotion' is described as crunchy and solid.
band_member_comments.Keys: Debate over piano – some claim Pigpen, others identify Ned Lagin playing cautiously in the background.
